title: Invocation Backcompat Concierge: runtime mapping & streaming semantics for OpenAI-style tools and legacy functions
creator: Ana Villarreal
description: Introduce a runtime-level 'concierge' layer that reconciles OpenAI-style tool invocation semantics and legacy function calls at request time. The concierge should: (1) map naming variants and aliases to a canonical identifier backed by a mutable registry, (2) perform protocol negotiation for streaming vs non-streaming invocations and produce consistent partial-call events, (3) translate parameter/argument shapes (including nested params encoded as JSON strings) with safe fallbacks, and (4) surface detailed telemetry and deterministic fallback traces for debugging and audits.
background: Multiple teams reported invocation failures when customers migrated from legacy 'functions' to OpenAI-style 'tools' or vice-versa. Root causes include name collisions, runtime-only aliasing, parameter shape mismatches, and inconsistent streaming partial-event semantics that break client-side reconcilers. Existing tickets touch parts of the problem (name registries, aliasing, invocation envelopes) but there is no single runtime layer orchestrating all fallbacks and telemetry for compatibility scenarios.
goals: Create a light-weight runtime mapping service (concierge) that resolves identifier aliases to canonical invocations at the edge
Ensure streaming partial-call events are consistent across protocols (OpenAI-style chunked toolcall events vs legacy function streaming)
Implement parameter translation rules with explicit, auditable fallbacks and schema validation
Emit rich telemetry and a deterministic fallback trace for each resolved invocation
non_goals: Designing a long-term global canonical registry UI (this will be a later product effort)
Changing persistent customer-facing tool/function names without explicit customer opt-in
Complex automated migration of user code; concierge only provides runtime compatibility
technical_design: Registry: lightweight JSON-backed alias table (in-memory with periodic persistence) mapping aliases, known variants, and semantic tags to canonical identifiers
Resolution algorithm: multi-stage pipeline: exact match -> normalized (case/underscore/dash) -> alias table lookup -> fuzzy suffix heuristic -> last-resort probabilistic match (only with telemetry)
Parameter translation: declarative adapters per canonical id describing accepted shapes, JSON coercions, and deprecation hints
Streaming semantics: define a canonical partial-call event envelope (concierge emits unified events for both styles with 'phase' metadata: start/partial/end/error)
Error mapping: map runtime/transport errors to a normalized error taxonomy with remediation hints to present to client SDKs
Fallback policy: configurable per-project policy (strict, permissive, warn-only) stored in deployment config
acceptance_criteria: Concierge resolves >99% of real invocation variants in the integration test corpus without modifying user payloads
Unified partial-call event schema emitted for both OpenAI-style and legacy streams (tests validate event ordering and completeness)
Parameter translation rules executed and logged; at least three canonical adapters implemented (example: dates, file blobs encoded as base64, nested param JSON-in-string)
Telemetry includes resolved canonical id, resolution path, applied translations, and fallback policy used; telemetry query dashboard created in Console for team to inspect
test_plan: Unit tests for resolution pipeline with synthesized alias sets
Integration harness using recorded customer traces (anonymized) to validate >99% resolution rate
Spike: end-to-end test that opens streaming connection with an OpenAI-style toolcall and verifies the unified events arrive to client SDKs
Chaos test: simulate concurrent alias table updates and ensure deterministic resolution within a request window
rollout_plan: Canary: runtime-1.24 small fleet with concierge in warn-only mode (no behavioral fallback, just telemetry) for 48 hours
Gradual: enable permissive mode for 5% traffic for 7 days and compare error rates and latency impact
Enable strict fallback for customers on migration track after explicit opt-in with a negotiated rollback plan
telemetry: Fields: canonical_id, resolution_path (pipe-delimited aliases), translations_applied, partial_event_counts, fallback_policy, latency_ms
Dashboards: per-canonical-id invocation counts, failure rates, and average resolution latency
Alerts: spike in probabilistic-match usage (>1%) or translation error rate (>0.5%)
risks: Performance: extra resolution step could increase P50/P95 latency; mitigation: optimize hot-path cache and adaptive batching
Incorrect fuzzy matches could route to wrong tool; mitigation: require conservative thresholds and warn-only default
Visibility: insufficient telemetry could make root-cause hard to debug; mitigation: high-cardinality fields initially sampled
implementation_steps: Design registry schema and in-memory cache layout
Implement resolution pipeline library with pluggable heuristics
Add parameter adapter DSL and three initial adapters for dates, base64 blobs, and JSON-in-string payloads
Implement streaming event unifier and canonical envelope emitter
Integrate concierge into edge request flow and wire telemetry
E2E tests, perf tuning, and canary rollout automation
